title: Aid Stations – Western States 100
claims: There are 20 aid stations, including 10 major medical checkpoints along the course.
With a staff of over 1,500 volunteers, the river crossing alone has a team of 125 personnel.
Western States is a cupless race.
The fluids generally available are water, GU Hydration Drink Tabs, ROCTANE Energy Drink, Sprite or 7Up and Coke; night aid stations also have soup, hot coffee and hot chocolate.
The foods generally available include saltines, pretzels, chips, GU gels, oranges, bananas, melons, potatoes, cookies, candies and sandwiches.
Hot soup is available at several aid stations, including the River Crossing, Auburn Lake Trails and Pointed Rocks.
Ibuprofen and Naprosyn are not provided at aid stations.
The medical staff includes approximately 50 physicians and 75 nurses, podiatrists, emergency medical technicians, paramedics and massage therapists.
Olympic Valley is mile 0, has medical cover and crew access in multiple places, and the race starts at 5:00 a.m.

Cut-off times reflect the deadlines for leaving the aid station and are strictly enforced; anyone leaving after the cut-off is disqualified.
Cut-offs marked with an asterisk are default cut-offs identical to the cut-off at the next aid station.
Cut-off times are not intended as a pacing guide.
Drop bags must fit through a 6 x 8 inch opening, be no longer than 16 inches, and are limited to one per aid station.
Drop bags are collected on the Friday before the Run between 9:00 a.m. and 1:00 p.m. near the corner of Squaw Peak and Squaw Valley Road.
Drop bags are returned to the Placer High School track and must be claimed by 3:00 p.m. Sunday.
